capitals.name: El Tajín
capitals.note: Infobox 20°26′53.01″N 97°22′41.67″W; 'by 600 CE, El Tajín was a city'; 'El Tajín flourished from 600 to 1200 AD'.

correction.text: controlled an area from between the Cazones and Tecolutla Rivers to the modern state of Puebla; years 600..704: 'Monumental construction started soon after and by 600 CE, El Tajín was a city'

keyframe_review.note: Redrawn (review fix, option a: keep the El Tajín reading). Cliopatria's shape does not contain El Tajín: the site (infobox 20°26′53″N 97°22′42″W) lies outside the bbox of all four shapes (-97.35..-96.38, 19.57..20.41), about 38 km from the nearest cell of the 555 shape, whose 17 cells centre on the Nautla-Misantla coast (about 19.94 N, 96.89 W); the 705 shape (58 cells) centres on the central Veracruz coast (about 19.37 N, 96.63 W); the page's core 'between the Cazones and Tecolutla Rivers' lies north of every shape. A 40 km circle around El Tajín shares 1 cell with the Cliopatria shape. Replaced by a 40 km radius around El Tajín (16 cells, about 4,600 km2 against Cliopatria's 5,463 km2; it reaches the Puebla border, 2 cells in Puebla), the researcher's reading of 'from between the Cazones and Tecolutla Rivers to the modern state of Puebla'. The shape Cliopatria drew belongs to the Classic Veracruz culture's coast (the culture page: 'between the Pánuco River on the north and the Papaloapan River on the south'), not to the city. Years: Cliopatria starts the row in 555; the page's first date for the city is 600, so 555-599 is dropped. 'The area was populated by the Huastec at the time the settlement was founded in the 1st century CE', a village, not a state. No infobox area to compare: the site is 1,056 ha in the text, 240 ha in the UNESCO box.

correction.text: El Tajín's core united with the Cliopatria 705 shape; years 705..1099: El Tajín 'eventually controlled much of what is now modern Veracruz state'; 'It reached its apogee in the Epi-Classic (900-1100 CE)'

keyframe_review.note: Redrawn (review fix, option a). The Cliopatria 705 shape (58 cells, 18,504 km2, reaching south to 18.54 N toward the central Veracruz coast) is consistent with 'eventually controlled much of what is now modern Veracruz state' ('From 600 to 1200 CE'), but it does not contain the city, so it is united with the 40 km core around El Tajín (73 cells). The page dates neither the expansion (Cliopatria's 705) nor its extent; the Totonac page, tried for a date, gives none either. Years trimmed to 1099 because the apogee ends in 1100 on the page; the ledger's 1100 loss follows.

correction.text: controlled an area from between the Cazones and Tecolutla Rivers to the modern state of Puebla; years 1100..1200: back to the core after the apogee (900-1100)

keyframe_review.note: Redrawn (review fix, option a). Cliopatria's 1111 shape is the same 17 cells as the 555 one (off the site; see classic-veracruz-culture_555), so it is replaced by the 40 km core around El Tajín. Years moved from 1111..1226 to 1100..1200: the apogee ends in 1100 and the city 'flourished from 600 to 1200 AD', then 'was destroyed by fire' in 'the early years of the 13th century'.

correction.text: not used: El Tajín 'prospered until the early years of the 13th century, when it was destroyed by fire'; the state ends in 1200 in this dossier

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 1227..1235 tail lies after the destruction and is the same off-site 17-cell shape as the 555 one (see classic-veracruz-culture_555). A loose reading of 'early years of the 13th century' could reach the 1230s, but the dossier ends the state at the page's 1200; see notes.

region.text: El Tajín and its surroundings, 'from between the Cazones and Tecolutla Rivers to the modern state of Puebla'

ledger.note: 600: El Tajín becomes a city. 'Monumental construction started soon after and by 600 CE, El Tajín was a city'; 'El Tajín flourished from 600 to 1200 AD'. The settlement itself dates from 'the 1st century CE', when 'the area was populated by the Huastec'. The year is the page's; the region is a 40 km radius around the site, the researcher's reading of the page's 'controlled an area from between the Cazones and Tecolutla Rivers to the modern state of Puebla' (undated there). Cliopatria's first shape lies off the site and is not used.

region.text: south along the Veracruz coast: 'eventually controlled much of what is now modern Veracruz state'

ledger.note: c. 705: El Tajín's control spreads south along the coast (Cliopatria's 705 keyframe, less the 40 km core). The page gives no date: El Tajín 'controlled an area from between the Cazones and Tecolutla Rivers to the modern state of Puebla' and 'From 600 to 1200 CE, El Tajín was a prosperous city that eventually controlled much of what is now modern Veracruz state'; 'El Tajín reached its peak after the fall of Teotihuacan'. The Totonac page, re-read for a date, has none (it gives only the 15th-century Totonacapan, 'roughly from Papantla in the north to Cempoala in the south'). Bridging event at confidence 1.

region.text: the southern coast beyond the 40 km core

ledger.note: 1100: the apogee ends and El Tajín's wider control lapses. 'It reached its apogee in the Epi-Classic (900-1100 CE)'. The year is the page's; the land is the 705 gain handed back, moved from Cliopatria's 1111 to 1100.

region.text: El Tajín and its core; 'destroyed by fire'

ledger.note: 1200: El Tajín is destroyed by fire and abandoned. 'El Tajín flourished from 600 to 1200 AD'; it 'prospered until the early years of the 13th century, when it was destroyed by fire' and 'was left to the jungle and remained covered and silent for over 500 years'. 'The Totonacs established the nearby settlement of Papantla after the fall of El Tajín' (no year on the Totonac page). Cliopatria runs the row to 1235 (an off-site shape).

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines; the southern extent is undated on the page.

notes: Cliopatria's 'Classic Veracruz Culture' row (555..1235, four shapes) has years that match El Tajín ('flourished from 600 to 1200 AD') but shapes that do not contain it (see the repair paragraph); the Classic Veracruz culture page runs 'from roughly 100 to 1000 CE' along the whole Gulf Coast 'between the Pánuco River on the north and the Papaloapan River on the south'. The dossier is therefore written as El Tajín (type state) under the Cliopatria slug; no 'el-tajin' slug was created (El Tajín is not in the orchestrator's list of states to add). The row is one continuous polity, not successive states, so it is not split. The culture as a whole (Cerro de las Mesas, Remojadas, Las Higueras, Zapotal; undated on its page) has no dossier; a culture-type dossier for central Veracruz 250–600 would fill the gap between epi-olmec-culture and El Tajín. End year: the page says 1200 ('flourished from 600 to 1200') and 'the early years of the 13th century' for the fire; 1200 is used and Cliopatria's 1227..1235 tail is marked wrong; a reviewer may prefer c. 1230 (common in the literature, not on the pages opened). The ethnic identity of the builders (Totonac or Huastec) is open on both pages. Pages opened: 3 of a budget of 5; Cliopatria has no Seshat id for this row. REPAIR 2026-10-18 (reviewer's fail, option a chosen): the earlier statement that the four shapes are 'centred on El Tajín' was wrong. The site is outside all four shapes (about 38 km from the nearest cell of the 555 shape, which centres on the Nautla-Misantla coast; the 705 shape centres on the central Veracruz coast; the page's core between the Cazones and Tecolutla Rivers is north of every shape). The El Tajín reading is kept because the years (600-1200, apogee 900-1100, fire early 13th century) are the city's, and the shapes are redrawn: 555, 1111 and 1227 shapes (the same 17 cells) become a 40 km radius around El Tajín (1227 stays wrong, being after the fire); the 705 shape is united with that circle. The ledger regions, the found, 705, 1100 and 1200 events, follow. Why not option b (the row as the culture plus an el-tajin slug): the row runs 555..1235, which fits neither the culture's 'roughly 100 to 1000 CE' nor a polity whose shapes sit on the central coast, and the culture would need its own multi-shape dossier from the Pánuco to the Papaloapan; a culture-type dossier for it remains a gap (listed among the counterparts needing dossiers). The Cliopatria shapes lie on the coast south of the Tecolutla and may be meant for the culture's coastal area rather than the city (a reading). Thin item: the date of the 705 southward expansion is still Cliopatria's (confidence 1); the Totonac page (re-read) has no date for it and no mention of the Tecolutla or Cazones rivers in connection with Totonacapan.
